bio: Prof. Dr. Srijan Lal Shrestha is Professor of Statistics and former Head of the Central Department of Statistics (CDS), Institute of Science and Technology, Tribhuvan University, where he has taught since 1992 and has been Professor since 2013. He earned his PhD in Statistics from TU in 2007, and since 2022 has also been Adjunct Faculty at Chandigarh University, India.

His research applies environmetrics, generalized linear models, time series and distributed lag methods to air pollution, climate-sensitive disease, drought and rainfall risk, population and human development in Nepal. He has authored or co-authored around three dozen research papers and reports, working with the WHO Urban Health Initiative, the Nepal Health Research Council and the Nepal Academy of Science and Technology. He has supervised one PhD to completion and co-supervised two more.

He is Editor-in-Chief of the Nepalese Journal of Statistics, an Academic Editor of PLOS ONE and a member of the Governing Board of the School of Mathematical Sciences, TU. He received the NABIL Science and Technology Award (2016) and the Nepal Bidhya Bhushan "KA" (2009), and held a NAST Climate Change Research Grant (2014–2016).

He is presently a Senior Visiting Professor in the MPhil programmes of Purbanchal University, Mid-West University and the School of Management, Tribhuvan University, and in the PhD programme of IoST, Tribhuvan University.

supervision.intro: Prof. Shrestha supervises MSc and PhD research in Statistics at the Central Department of Statistics, IoST, Tribhuvan University. He has supervised one PhD to completion, co-supervised two more, and has three PhD supervisions or co-supervisions under way. Prospective scholars with an interest in applied and environmental statistics are welcome to get in touch with a short research outline.
areas: Environmetrics and air quality modeling (PM2.5 / PM10)
Environmental epidemiology and burden of disease
Climate, drought and rainfall risk modeling
Time series and distributed lag models
Human development indices and socio-economic measurement
steps: Read two or three recent papers in the area you want to work on.
Prepare a one-page outline: question, data source and the methods you expect to use.
Send it through the contact form or by email, mentioning MSc or PhD.

publications.title: Enhancement of Human Development Assessment Model: An Insight from Bagmati Province, Nepal
publications.summary: Extends the HDI with social governance and technological adaptation, weighted by principal component analysis; a 2023 survey of 569 households puts Bagmati Province's HDI at 0.524, well below the UNDP figure of 0.661.

publications.title: An investigation of factors associated with the ecological footprint in Nepal through statistical modeling
publications.summary: Statistical modeling of the economic, demographic and energy factors associated with Nepal's ecological footprint.

publications.title: Five-dimensional unequally weighted mapping methodology for measuring the level of human development: an application in Bagmati Province, Nepal
publications.summary: Introduces a five-dimensional, unequally weighted mapping method for measuring subnational human development, illustrated for Bagmati Province.

publications.title: Modeling the ecological footprint and assessing its influential factors: A systematic review
publications.summary: Systematic review of statistical approaches to modeling the ecological footprint and the factors that drive it.

publications.title: Assessing Human Development in Nepal through Descriptive and Cluster Analysis: Progress and Disparities
publications.journal: Applied Research in Quality of Life
publications.summary: Uses descriptive statistics and cluster analysis to track progress and regional disparities in human development across Nepal.

publications.title: Burden of Respiratory Diseases Attributable to Household Air Pollution in Nepal: National and Provincial Estimates
publications.summary: Applies WHO methods to estimate the share of childhood pneumonia, ARI and COPD/asthma attributable to household air pollution in 2019/20, nationally and by province; rural areas and Karnali Province are worst affected.

publications.title: Quantifying effects of meteorological parameters on air pollution in Kathmandu valley through regression models
publications.summary: Regression models quantifying how temperature, humidity, wind and rainfall shape air pollution levels in Kathmandu Valley.

publications.title: Effects of Climatic Factors on Diarrheal Diseases among Children below 5 Years of Age at National and Subnational Levels in Nepal: An Ecological Study
publications.journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
publications.summary: Time-series models of 2002–2014 district data show diarrheal disease in Nepal rising 4.4% per 1 °C of mean temperature and 0.28% per cm of rainfall, with the strongest effects in mountain regions.

publications.title: Curvilinear and gamma generalized linear models for modeling the dependency of air pollution levels on meteorological conditions in Kathmandu valley
publications.journal: Research Square (preprint; WHO Urban Health Initiative study)
publications.summary: Exponential, Box-Cox and gamma GLMs on 2017–2020 daily data explain 79–85% of the variation in Kathmandu Valley air pollution and quantify the effects of temperature, humidity, rainfall and wind.

publications.title: Assessment of Factors Associated with Indoor Air Pollution using Multinomial Logistic Regression: A Case Study of Barbardiya Municipality
publications.summary: Multinomial logistic regression on 370 households links ethnicity, the household head's education and income to high indoor air pollution in Barbardiya Municipality.

publications.title: Air pollution exposure and health impacts in the Kathmandu valley
publications.journal: International Journal of Environment and Health
publications.summary: Reviews air pollution monitoring in Kathmandu Valley since 2003, which shows a substantial fall in particulate pollution, and the associated health impacts.

publications.title: Analysis of ambient particulate air pollution and health in Nepal
publications.journal: Journal of Global Ecology and Environment
publications.summary: Analysis of ambient particulate matter levels in Nepal and their relationship with health outcomes.

publications.title: Trend Analysis, Modelling and Impact Assessment of COVID-19 in Nepal
publications.journal: Journal of Institute of Science and Technology
publications.summary: Trend analysis and statistical modeling of the early COVID-19 epidemic in Nepal, with an assessment of its impact.

publications.title: Assessment of Ambient Particulate Air Pollution and its Attribution to Burden of Disease in Kathmandu Valley, Nepal: A Review
publications.summary: Review of ambient particulate pollution in Kathmandu Valley and the share of disease burden attributable to it.

publications.title: A probabilistic approach for assessment of future drought in Bagmati River Basin, Nepal
publications.summary: Probabilistic assessment of future drought occurrence in the Bagmati River Basin.

publications.title: Negative Binomial Model in Linking Water-borne and Vector-borne Disease Hospitalizations with Climate Sensitive Variables in Nepal
publications.summary: Negative binomial models linking hospitalizations for water-borne and vector-borne diseases to climate-sensitive variables in Nepal.

publications.title: Statistical Modeling of Health Effects on Climate-Sensitive Variables and Assessment of Environmental Burden of Diseases Attributable to Climate Change in Nepal
publications.summary: Models health outcomes against climate-sensitive variables and estimates the environmental burden of disease attributable to climate change in Nepal.

publications.title: Seasonally Separated Logistic Models to Assess the Impact of Climate Variables on Occurrence of Rainfall over the Bagmati River Basin of Nepal
publications.journal: British Journal of Environment and Climate Change
publications.summary: Season-specific logistic models for the effect of climate variables on rainfall occurrence over the Bagmati River Basin.

publications.title: Region-wise Effects of Climate Sensitive Variables on Some Specific Disease Burdens in Nepal
publications.summary: Region-by-region estimates of how climate-sensitive variables affect specific disease burdens across Nepal.

publications.title: Logistic Model as a Statistical Downscaling Approach for Forecasting a Wet or Dry Day in the Bagmati River Basin
publications.summary: Uses a logistic model as a statistical downscaling approach to forecast wet and dry days in the Bagmati River Basin.

publications.title: Dynamics of Population Ageing in Nepal and the Need for Action
publications.summary: Analyses the dynamics of population ageing in Nepal and the policy action it calls for.

publications.title: Censored Negative Exponential Distribution as a Mixed Distribution and Derivation of Its Moments
publications.journal: Nepal Journal of Science and Technology
publications.summary: Treats the censored negative exponential distribution as a mixed distribution and derives its moments.

publications.title: Poisson Model for Linking Children Ever Born with Some Key Predictor Variables in Nepalese Women
publications.journal: Journal of Institute of Science and Technology
publications.summary: Poisson regression linking the number of children ever born to key socio-demographic predictors among Nepalese women.

publications.title: Particulate air pollution and daily mortality in Kathmandu Valley, Nepal: associations and distributed lag

publications.title: Statistical Models and Water Quality Characterization of Source Waters in Nepal

publications.title: Statistical Analysis of Factors Associated with Maternal Mortality in Nepal

publications.journal: International Journal of Environment and Pollution
publications.summary: Statistical models of health effects linked to kitchen exposure to indoor air pollution, from a cross-sectional household survey in Nepal.

publications.title: Indoor air pollution from biomass fuels and respiratory health of the exposed population in Nepalese households
publications.journal: International Journal of Occupational and Environmental Health
publications.summary: Household study of indoor air pollution from biomass fuels and respiratory health among exposed household members.

publications.title: Application of Triple Exponential Smoothing Technique in the Analysis of Time Series with a Quadratic Trend
publications.journal: Nepal Journal of Science and Technology
publications.summary: Applies triple exponential smoothing to the analysis and forecasting of time series with a quadratic trend.
